messages.content: How can I sell my acoustic guitar?

function.name: tune_instrument
function.description: This function helps tune instruments based on the instrument type and the desired key or note. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

instrument_type.description: The type of the instrument, e.g. 'acoustic guitar', 'piano'.

key.description: The key or note to which the instrument should be tuned to. Default is 'Standard' for guitars.

message.content:
Here’s a quick, step‑by‑step guide to help you get your acoustic guitar sold quickly and for a fair price: | Step | What to Do | Why It Matters | |------|------------|----------------| | **1. Clean & Tune** | Give the guitar a good wipe‑down, polish the finish, and tune it to standard pitch. | A well‑maintained instrument looks more appealing and shows buyers you’ve cared for it. | | **2. Take High‑Quality Photos** | Shoot from multiple angles (headstock, body, back, neck, strings). Use natural light and a neutral background. | Great photos attract more views and help justify your asking price. | | **3. Research Market Value** | Check recent sales on Reverb, eBay, Craigslist, and local classifieds. Look at similar models, ages, and conditions. | Knowing the going rate prevents over‑pricing or under‑pricing. | | **4. Write a Clear Listing** | Include:
• Brand, model, year, serial number (if known)
• Condition notes (scratches, repairs, original parts)
• Any extras (case, strap, accessories)
• Reason for selling | Transparency builds trust and reduces back‑and‑forth questions. | | **5. Choose Your Platforms** | • **Reverb** – great for musical gear, buyer protection.
• **eBay** – broad audience, auction or fixed price.
• **Craigslist / Facebook Marketplace** – local, no shipping hassles.
• **Local music stores** – consignment or direct purchase. | Different platforms reach different buyer types; use a mix for maximum exposure. | | **6. Set a Competitive Price** | Start slightly above your target price to allow room for negotiation. | Buyers often expect to haggle; a buffer keeps you from underselling. | | **7. Decide on Shipping vs. Local Pickup** | • **Shipping**: Use a sturdy case, bubble wrap, and a reputable carrier with tracking.
• **Pickup**: Meet in a public place, bring a friend, and bring a small amount of cash or a secure payment method. | Shipping expands your market but adds cost; pickup saves money but requires safety precautions. | | **8. Handle Payment Securely** | • For local sales: cash or Venmo/PayPal (with buyer protection).
• For online sales: PayPal Goods & Services, or a platform‑provided escrow. | Protects both parties from fraud. | | **9. Close the Sale** | Once payment is confirmed, hand over the guitar, provide any paperwork (if applicable), and keep a record of the transaction. | A smooth hand‑off leaves a positive impression and protects you legally. | | **10. Optional: Trade‑In or Consignment** | If you’re not in a hurry, consider trading the guitar at a local shop or consigning it for a commission. | You may get a better price or a hassle‑free sale. | ### Quick Tips - **Be Honest**: Disclose any damage or repairs. Honesty builds buyer confidence and reduces disputes. - **Use a Consistent Description**: Keep the same wording across all listings to avoid confusion. - **Respond Promptly**: Answer inquiries within 24 hours to keep potential buyers engaged. - **Safety First**: For in‑person meetings, choose a well‑lit, public location and bring a friend if possible. ### Sample Listing Snippet > **2010 Yamaha FG800 Acoustic Guitar – Excellent Condition** > • 12‑string nylon, 25.5” scale, natural finish > • Minor scratch on the back, no cracks or repairs needed > • Comes with a hard case, strap, and extra strings > • Price: $350 (negotiable) > • Local pickup in [City] or shipping available (buyer pays). Feel free to tweak the details to match your guitar’s specifics. Good luck with your sale!
